title: Retries
description: Which requests and statuses are retried, the backoff, Retry-After, and the limits (clients/spec/README.md, section 3.4).

cases.description: A GET that gets 408 is sent again after 0.5 seconds (jitter 0), and the second answer is the result.
A GET that gets 429 is sent again after 0.5 seconds (jitter 0), and the second answer is the result.
A GET that gets 500 is sent again after 0.5 seconds (jitter 0), and the second answer is the result.
A GET that gets 502 is sent again after 0.5 seconds (jitter 0), and the second answer is the result.
A GET that gets 503 is sent again after 0.5 seconds (jitter 0), and the second answer is the result.
A GET that gets 504 is sent again after 0.5 seconds (jitter 0), and the second answer is the result.
Two retries by default, so three attempts, with the delays 0.5 and 1 seconds; then the last error goes to the caller.

cases.description: The delay is min(8, 0.5 * 2^(n-1)) * (1 - 0.25 * jitter): with jitter 0.5, 0.4375 and 0.875 seconds.
With max_retries 6 the delays double up to the cap of 8 seconds: 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 8.
max_retries 0 on the client turns the retries off.

cases.description: max_retries of one call wins over the client: 1 retry, so two attempts.

cases.description: Retry-After in whole seconds wins over the backoff delay.
Retry-After as an HTTP date is read against the injected clock: 7 seconds after now.
A Retry-After above 60 seconds ends the retries: the error goes to the caller at once.
A connection error (no response) is retried.
After the last attempt a connection error becomes ConnectionError.
A POST that carries an Idempotency-Key is retried, with the same key.
409 idempotency_in_progress is retried with the same key.
